tagline.text: Climb through a limestone rock in the rice fields, then ride a zipline back down

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Tagabinet, Puerto Princesa (along the Puerto Princesa–Sabang road)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱450–700 (per person, admission/cave climb and zipline only, excluding transport)

children.text: Ugong Rock is a limestone outcrop about 23 m high that rises from the rice fields of Barangay Tagabinet, on the road from Puerto Princesa to Sabang, home of the Underground River. Run by a village cooperative, the experience takes you up through cracks and ladders inside the rock to the summit, then down by zipline, and it is usually combined with an Underground River tour.
Ugong Rock sits in Barangay Tagabinet, Puerto Princesa, on Palawan Island. It stands beside the national highway that runs north from Puerto Princesa toward Sabang, about
1 hour 20 minutes
by road from the city and about
20 minutes
before the Sabang wharf. Its height is often given as about 75 feet (about

), though some articles claim it is taller, so the exact figure varies by source. Looking up from the foot of the rock, a lone lump of limestone rising out of fields and forest is an impressive sight.

"Ugong" means a humming or resonating sound in Filipino. The rock is said to be named for its hollow interior, which rings when tapped, and along the way guides knock on parts of the rock so you can hear sounds like a bell or a drum. The rock is a community-based tourism project run by the Tagabinet Ugong Rock Multipurpose Cooperative, so the guides are villagers and the fees go to the cooperative. At first it offered caving only, and the zipline is said to have been added around 2011 as demand grew.

The experience is simple. After a safety briefing and receiving a helmet and gloves, you enter at the bottom of the rock with a guide and climb through ropes, wooden stairs, ladders and narrow gaps all the way to the top. One section has a short rope climb, and some spots require twisting your body to squeeze through. The climb usually takes
20–45 minutes
, longer if it is hot and humid. From the summit you look over rice fields, the karst ridge and the village, and you can come down either by zipline or by returning the way you came.

Ugong Rock is less a place to admire beautiful stalactite caves than an adventure of moving through the inside of a rock with your own body. It fits neatly into an hour or two before or after an Underground River (Puerto Princesa Underground River) tour, and because guides help along the way, it suits beginner adventurers even if you are not very fit. Because you have to pass through tight spots, think ahead if you are claustrophobic or have knee or back problems.

Starting at the entrance at the base of the rock, you climb to the summit through ropes, ladders, wooden stairs and narrow gaps. A guide leads you through passages where bats and swiftlets live. No previous climbing-gear experience is needed.

blocks.title: The sound of the ringing rock

children.text: This is the part that gave the rock its name. When a guide knocks on part of the rock, the hollow section rings like a bell or a drum. Some guides invite you to try it yourself, but cave formations such as stalactites must not be touched by hand.
A 360-degree view takes in the fields, the village and the karst ridges in the distance. It is also a place to cool down and rest after the climb. On a clear morning the photos come out well.
From the summit you come down on a zipline stretched far over the fields. You can ride seated or face-down in the "Superman" position, and many sources give the length as about
with a ride of just over
30 seconds
. You choose the style when you register before setting out.

The guides are Tagabinet residents. Before setting out they say a short prayer, explain the safety rules and then go with you. They tell you where to put your hands and feet, so simply following their instructions keeps things manageable.

blocks.title: A convenient stop on the Underground River route

children.text: It lies about
20 minutes
before the Sabang wharf, so it is easy to slot into an Underground River tour. Many tours include it on the way to or from the Underground River.

Nearby is a karst rock called Elephant Cave that is said to look like an elephant, and it is described as a quick photo stop. Reviews say it takes some imagination, so only stop if you have spare time.

items.title: A day combined with the Underground River
items.subtitle: Day trip from the city toward Sabang

children.text: Leave your hotel in Puerto Princesa by tour vehicle and head north toward Sabang. Entry to the Underground River requires an advance permit, so book ahead.
Take a bangka boat through the Underground River from Sabang (the order may shift depending on your permit time).
Have lunch in Sabang, then stop at Ugong Rock in Tagabinet on the way back toward the city.
Register and pay the fees, then take the safety briefing and receive a helmet and gloves. Allow about
30–45 minutes
for the cave climb.
Rest at the summit, then ride the zipline down. Closing time is reported as somewhere between 4 PM and 5 PM, so do not arrive too late.
Return to the city and have dinner at a seafood restaurant.
This schedule is just one example. Many itineraries go to Ugong Rock first in the early morning to match the Underground River permit time.

items.title: A half day at Ugong Rock only
items.subtitle: Round trip from the city

children.text: Leave the city by Sabang-bound van or chartered vehicle and get off at Tagabinet.
Register when it opens (usually 8 AM). Mornings are cooler and less crowded.
Climb through the rock. Decide at the end whether to ride the zipline or climb back down.
Take a quick look at nearby Elephant Cave, then flag down a passing van or return to the city in a chartered vehicle.
Public transport is infrequent, so it is safer to arrange your ride back in advance.
A direct flight from Manila (NAIA) to Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS) takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change often, so check when you book.
The airport is fairly close to the city, and from the city you continue to Ugong Rock by road.

items.title: From the city to Ugong Rock

children.text: According to the city tourism office, take a Sabang-bound jeepney or shuttle from the San Jose terminal and ask the driver to drop you at Tagabinet. The fare is listed at about
The trip takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
Chartering an air-conditioned van is listed at about
or more for up to 10 people (through licensed tourist transport providers; it varies by season).
Underground River tours and hotel tour packages usually include the vehicle. If you go independently, return rides can be scarce, so check ahead.

items.title: As a stop on an Underground River tour

children.text: Most travelers visit as one stop on an Underground River tour. The tour price often includes the admission fee, but the zipline is usually not included.
When booking, check whether Ugong Rock is on the itinerary and whether admission and the zipline are included.

The dry season in Puerto Princesa runs roughly from December to May. The rock is less slippery then and the risk of rain disrupting your plans is small, so this is the best time to visit Ugong Rock. Days are hot and humid, though, and you sweat a lot climbing inside the rock, so go early in the morning.

During the June–November rainy season, showers and changes to Underground River tours are frequent, so plans can shift. Wet rock and ladders are slippery, so follow the local conditions that day and the guide's judgment. Opening hours differ by source, from 8 AM to 4 PM or 5 PM, so arrive well before closing.

There is almost no lodging around Ugong Rock, so most people make a day trip from hotels in Puerto Princesa or near Sabang. The city has hotels at every price level and tours are easy to arrange, so if you want to combine the Underground River and Ugong Rock in one day, it is easiest to leave early from the city.

Meals are often lunch at a restaurant near the Sabang wharf as part of the tour schedule. There may be places near the Ugong Rock entrance that sell simple drinks and snacks, but check the menu locally. Back in the city, Puerto Princesa's seafood restaurants are a good way to end the day.
Wear shoes with good grip (sneakers or trekking shoes). Sandals are dangerous on wet rock.
Wear comfortable clothes you do not mind getting dirty; long pants help because your knees and elbows can get scraped.
Do not carry things in your hands while climbing. Keep your bag close to your body or hand it over as the guide tells you; in narrow sections bags are sometimes passed through separately.
Helmets and gloves are usually lent out, so pick them up on site, and bring your own drinking water.
You choose whether to ride the zipline when you register, so prepare yourself mentally in advance. The seated style is less demanding.
Do not touch cave formations or walls by hand. Notices explain that oils and dirt from hands damage the formations.
Climbing in the morning is less hot and the summit view is better. Fix your Underground River permit time first so the two do not overlap.
There are narrow gaps and ladder sections, so it is not recommended if you are claustrophobic or have knee, back or hip problems; some sources also mention a weight limit, so check when you register.
Some sources mention a weight limit of about 120 kg. The standard may differ by section, so ask staff when you register.
Young children (under about 8) may find the ladders and tight spaces hard, according to reviews, so guardians should judge.
Fees and hours differ between older and recent sources, and no official fee sheet is available online. Check the local fee sheet and the latest notices.
Some reviews say older visitors get a blood-pressure check at the entrance, but I could not confirm whether it applies to every visitor.
When it rains, the rock and ladders are slippery. If the guide advises stopping, follow that advice.
A world-famous underground river national park entered by bangka from the Sabang wharf. It lies about
20 minutes
ahead of Ugong Rock by car and requires an advance permit.
Palawan's central city, with the airport, lodging and restaurants, and the starting point for the trip to Ugong Rock.
An island-hopping area reached by boat from a pier near the city. It is hard to combine with the Underground River and Ugong Rock on the same day.

A karst rock shaped like an elephant right next to Ugong Rock, and Sabang, the coastal village where Underground River boats depart. Sabang is also said to offer other activities such as a mangrove paddle and a zipline.
